Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned and sanitized at a regular frequency.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed. 
1. An accumulation of grease was observed under the fryers.
2. There were several tiles observed missing under the fryers. The area had been filled with bare concrete that is continuously absorbing the grease and accumulating soil and dust including food debris.
3. An accumulation of ice was observed int he walk-in freezer.
 Discussed with the PIC. The PIC assured inspector that the accumulations will be cleaned and the relevant repairs will be done.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

(C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The magnetic knife strip above the triple sink is observed to have rusted and is in direct contact with the food contact surface of the knife on it. This knife was pulled from service and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure this magnetic knife strip is removed and replaced if desired to have this piece of equipment in use. If this item does not want to be used in the facility, then the magnetic knife strip can simply be removed and then any holes in the wall can be patched. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: In the walk-in freezer there are multiple boxes observed stored directly on the floor. When brought to the PIC’s attention, employees were immediately instructed to relocate the boxes off the floor. Ensure that food storage takes place in these locations where the boxes are stored at least 6 inches off the floor. 
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The bottom shelf of the fry freezer and the external surface/gaskets of the fry freezer are observed with an accumulation of food debris. The top of the fry warmer is also observed with an accumulation of food debris/grease. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned and sanitized to remove the current accumulation of food debris/grease and then are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:

-The sandwich prep cooler under the lid near the back wall.
-The ice cream machine has a visible spill on the containers inside the cooler part of the machine.
Ensure these locations receive proper attention to detail when cleaning and are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. This is a repeated violation form the 4/24/2023 inspection and the facility will receive a Notice to Correct to document the violation. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.comment:

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: The fry freezer gasket is observed to be in a state of disrepair where the gasket has rolled over and exposed a gap where food accumulation is occurring. Ensure this area is cleaned of the food accumulation and that the gasket is repaired to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The wall and areas surrounding the hand sink near the ice cream is observed to have an accumulation of food debris/soils. Ensure the current accumulation is cleaned and sanitized to remove the current accumulation and then ensure the surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment: 2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by: (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: There was observed an employee beverage stored on top of the hot holding wells that could pose a potential contamination of the food items if spilt. The drink was removed from this location and placed on a back shelf that is designated for employee use. Ensure employees store drink items appropriately in a manner that does not pose a contamination hazard.
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: Employees were observed switching various task as, touching personal items, such as clothing and phones, and then engaging in food prep activities without properly washing their hands. PIC was informed about this violation and verbal education was provided to the employees during the inspection. Ensure employees wash their hands for the required amount of time and when appropriate such as after touching contaminated items.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: There was observed a spray bottle with a blue liquid that did not bare a label of the common name nor any identifiers. This bottle was identified by the PIC as window cleaner.  A label was placed on the bottle with the common name of “window cleaner”. Ensure that bottles are labeled properly for identification when taken from bulk containers and stored in a new container.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: There was a wiping cloth stored on the counter of the ice cream prep table during the inspection. The cloth was left in place for an extended period of time and not placed back into the sanitizer solution. PIC was made aware and the cloth was placed back into the sanitizer solution. PIC educated staff on the use of wiping cloths and their need to be stored in the solution between uses. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored in the sanitizer solution between use.
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

-The ice machine surface was observed to have an accumulation of food debris and other materials, especially in the tight to reach places.
-The hot holding wells are observed to have an accumulation of grease on the inside walls of the well.
-The sandwich prep cooler under the lid near the back wall.
-The ketchup dispenser on the wall is observed to have an accumulation of food debris.
-The holder for the can opener is observed to have food and debris accumulation.
-The ice cream machine has a visible spill on the containers inside the cooler part of the machine.
Ensure these locations receive proper attention to detail when cleaning and are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

-under/around the ice machine
-around the drive thru
-and around the triple sink corner on the floor and the caulking.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.comment:

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. 3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.comment: Hand washing sinks are slow draining. Front three compartment sink faucet is leaking when off and draining onto the floor at times. Repair plumbing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15  (C) The plumbing needs repair. Repair according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed the ice bin at the drive thru window to be stored in the open position when not in use. Store ice bin closed in between use.
750-130 Ready to eat food shall be stored in a matter to prevent cross-contamination.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee eating at the service line and leaving leftover food on a tray that is used for the public. Food was discarded and tray was taken to the dish area. Employees may only eat in designated areas away from food and food prep areas.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the tabletop fan with dust accumulation, 2) the shelves in the reach in cooler on the cook line with grease and food debris accumulation. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service items to have been delivered via key drop delivery and placed right in front of the ice machine, where there is melting ice on the floor that is getting the boxes all wet. Single service items must be stored at least 6" off of the floor. In the event of key drop deliveries, make sure these items are put away in designated areas as soon as possible and protect them from contamination in the meantime.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the drain pipe underneath the front small three compartment sink to splash and pool water on the floor in this area. Re-position pipe so that water drains effectively but make sure to maintain air gap.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
The mix n chill was soiled with food debris. Wash, rinse, and sanitize food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The top of the ice machine where the ice deflector meets the top of the machine was soiled with what appears to be mold. Clean non food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:

750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean

750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed

Observed coffee filters stored out in the open. Store coffee filters in a covered container or in a manner that prevents them from possible contamination.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:

750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No employee on staff currently has an IL FSSMC. The new GM, Daniel, stated that he has taken the FSSMC through ServSafe and has to submit his fee to the state to obtain his state certificate. Follow up in 90 days.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
1.  The vent fans in both bathrooms do not work.  Repair or replace the fans.
2.  There was no soap at the hand sink in the dish washing area.  Soap was put in the dispenser during the inspection to CORRECT the violation.

750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Outside storage area clean, enclosure properly constructed
findings.comment:
The concrete pad inside the dumpster enclosure had debris on it.  Remove the debris.

750-1140c Outside storage areas shall be large enough to store the outside garbage and refuse containers and shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The following floors were soiled, or in need of repair, or the coving was damaged:
  1.  Almost all the floor drains in the facility were soiled (covers and inside them).  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  2.  There was puddling water under the front 3-pan sink (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  3.  The grout was low and soiled between the floor tiles in front of the 3-pan sink in back (REPEAT VIOLATION)  and in front of the fryers and grill.
  4.  Grout was missing at the top of the coving to the left of the back 3-pan sink  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  5.  The floor in front of the ice cream machine was soiled.
  6.  The floor under the racks in the  (A) walk-in freezer, and (B) walk-in cooler were soiled.
  7.  The coving was pulled away from the wall with food debris in the gap on the wall (A) behind the hamburger grill,   (B) to the left of the hamburger freezer next to the grill,  and (C) behind the French fry warmer and steam wells on the cook line.  
  8.  The floor to the left and right of the soda dispenser near the drive up window was soiled.
  9.  The floor under the soda dispenser to the right of the front 3-pan sink was soiled.
  10. The threshold under the exterior door near the drive-up window was soiled.

750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross

2.  Roller skates and aprons were stored on shelving near the back exterior door above boxes of food handling gloves and straws.

750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
1.  The water heater room near the back exterior door was soiled and cluttered with what appeared to be broken or unused equipment and other refuse.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)  Clean the room, its contents, and discard all unused equipment and refuse.
2.  A mop was stored in the mop sink with the mop head laying in the sink.  Store the mop with the head up where it will air dry.

750-1350c Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items.  750-1350a Food service establishments and all parts of property used in connection with their operation shall be kept free of litter.  Remove all unnecessary items.  750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.
